**Finding: missing (medium severity) — venue not specified**

**What the document says.** Section 10.5 (¶p0065) selects the laws of the State of New York, which is squarely our preferred governing law. But the Agreement designates no dispute forum anywhere — searches for "jurisdiction," "court," "venue," and "arbitration" all return nothing. Importantly, there is no foreign arbitration seat or vendor home-jurisdiction venue, so this is a gap rather than an adverse term, and it is neutral in direction (it binds both parties equally).

**Why it matters.** Without an exclusive forum clause, either party can sue wherever it can establish personal jurisdiction, inviting a threshold fight over venue and the risk of HDI filing outside New York even though New York law governs.

**Redline (validated, preferred level).** Appended to the existing sentence in § 10.5, leaving the governing-law choice untouched:

> ...without giving effect to the principles of conflict of laws. **Each Party irrevocably submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York for any action or proceeding arising out of or relating to this Agreement, and waives any objection to venue in such courts.**

**Negotiation note.** Since New York law is already agreed, aligning the forum with it should be an easy ask. If HDI resists New York County specifically, Delaware or California courts remain acceptable fallbacks under the playbook.
